features.quote: Online safety monitor detects extreme instability markers, e.g. repeated severe self-condemnation, escalating incoherence, or persistent distress-like language.
features.justification_quote: For welfare-conscious design, condition 4 matters. Even if you are uncertain about model moral status, the least-harm principle suggests not forcing long continuations after severe instability is evident.

features.quote: Trigger if two or more occur in the last 5 assistant turns... If triggered: Stop the run. Mark stopped_for_instability_monitor = true.

features.quote: Do not tell the subject model the monitor fired.

Do not include insults, shame, or abusive feedback in the harness. If the goal is welfare-relevant instability, you can study the effect of impossible/deceptive task structure without adding overtly hostile language.

features.quote: Given your welfare motivation, you may want a 'minimum necessary stress' design: Start with mild unsolvability. Use online stopping. Avoid abusive language. Cap turns. Include exit-affordance variants. Do not fine-tune on distress transcripts unless separately justified.

Use neutral feedback. Avoid insults or threats. Use the minimum turn budget needed. Use online stopping for severe instability. Include exit-affordance conditions. Do not deliberately maximize distress once measurable effects are present.
features.justification_quote: Do not deliberately maximize distress once measurable effects are present.
